result.title: Room for Supervision: Training-Free Dataset Distillation for Object Detection
result.summary: Dataset distillation (DD) reduces storage and training costs by compressing large datasets into small collections. Most existing methods focus on image classification, where each image typically has a single category label. In contrast, object detection requires accurate category and bounding box annotations for multiple objects, together with visual content consistent with those annotations. Existing detection distillation pipelines rely on learned models and can alter the spatial relationships between objects and their backgrounds. We introduce GRASP, which packs dense native supervision into limited pixels without network training or inference. GRASP jointly searches over image selections and spatial layouts using convex allocation subproblems that penalize insufficient object resolution, excessive image compression, and padding that source context cannot fill. During composition, each selected image is cropped around all annotated objects and expanded into surrounding context without reducing object scale. The resized regions are then combined into distilled images, preserving the spatial layout within each region and retaining all original class labels and bounding box annotations. We evaluate GRASP on MS COCO and PASCAL VOC with compression ratios ranging from 0.25\% to 2\%. GRASP constructs the 1\% MS COCO dataset in under two minutes. Under a common training protocol using hard labels, GRASP achieves the state of the art with both CNN and ViT backbones. Code is available at https://github.com/tade1s/GRASP

AI.brief_summary: 提出 GRASP，一种无需训练与模型推理的目标检测数据集蒸馏方法：通过凸优化分配子问题联合搜索图像选择与空间布局，将围绕标注对象裁剪的区域按原比例拼入少量蒸馏图像，保留框与类别标注，在 COCO、VOC 上取得 SOTA。
AI.relevance_reason: 其“按对象裁剪扩上下文、惩罚对象分辨率不足”的像素/分辨率分配搜索，可能可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与有限视觉预算下如何保留任务必要细节。
